clue.text: Shock to receive refusal about it from caretaker

indicators.note: the word for shock takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to jar is to jolt or shock

indicators.note: the refusal word sits around the clue's word it

explanation.surface: A caretaker gets a nasty jolt when someone refuses to deal with a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building, the job of a caretaker.

clue.text: Magistrate buttonholes university lecturer with energy drink

indicators.note: to buttonhole someone is to grab and hold them, so the magistrate's letters hold the rest

parts.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace, a magistrate
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A magistrate corners an academic who is clutching an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, as in the bourbon-and-mint cocktail.

clue.text: Closely storing a lot of nonsense in the cloud?

definitions.note: adjective: relating to a nebula, a cloud of gas in space

indicators.note: the word for closely keeps the other piece inside it
most of the word, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a pile of rubbish being kept in cloud storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to computer cloud storage; the definition means a cloud of dust and gas in space, the question mark flagging the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is an interstellar cloud, so nebular describes what relates to or sits inside such a cloud.

clue.text: Working in retail, securing name over a number of years

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
working means in operation, worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retail worker has kept their name on the books for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like part of the surface job but rearranges the two words that follow it; 'securing' then places the name letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial means lasting or recurring over a span of three years, a number of years.

clue.text: One's active in study of rationality

definitions.note: adjectival phrase: marked by sound logic

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: active suggests lively movement, so the letters of one's are stirred up

explanation.surface: A student is busy reading up on rational thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' is the anagram signal, turning the letters of One's into SONE; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasoned is logically argued, showing the quality of rational thinking.

clue.text: Document about English and British affected by fever

indicators.note: the document word goes round the other letters

explanation.surface: A report on English and British people suffering a feverish illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile is the medical adjective for feverish, from Latin febris.

clue.text: Celebration in France is held by motor-racing authority

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the authority's initials

parts.note: the FIA is the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile, which governs Formula One

explanation.surface: A celebration in France gets organised by the body that runs motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive holiday or party, especially in Spanish-speaking lands.

clue.text: Security required around Saint, Russian Saint

indicators.note: the security word wraps round the saint's letter

parts.note: bail is money given as security for an accused's return

explanation.surface: Guards are posted around a Russian saint's shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Basil is honoured in Moscow's St Basil's Cathedral on Red Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil the Blessed is a Russian holy fool after whom the Moscow cathedral is named.

clue.text: One unblemished after involving publicity team to produce publisher's mark

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for unblemished takes the team's letters into it

parts.note: in mint condition means unblemished, as new
PR is public relations, a publicity team

explanation.surface: A spotless reputation, after the PR people got involved, becomes a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is the name a publisher prints on its books, a trade mark of the house.

clue.text: European country and its neighbour study peace proposal

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NI is Northern Ireland, which borders Eire
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Two neighbouring countries in Europe examine a peace plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Ireland and Northern Ireland are a fitting backdrop for a peace proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon, from Greek eirene, is a proposal aiming to reconcile, a plan for harmony.

clue.text: Get drunk — Cuba libre (time for a Bishop to get drunk)

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the altered letters are scrambled
one B, the chess symbol for a bishop, is replaced by T, the symbol for time

explanation.surface: An instruction to get drunk on rum and cola, with a quirky bracketed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuba libre is rum and cola. 'time for a Bishop' changes a B to T, giving CUTALIBRE, which 'to get drunk' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricated is slang for tipsy, so to lubricate oneself is to drink until merry.

clue.text: Very good meal with no repeated component

indicators.note: the word for meal has a doubled letter, and one of the pair is dropped

explanation.surface: A splendid dinner where no dish turns up twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Supporter to arrive with many others, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to pile on is to crowd in en masse

explanation.surface: A fan turns up as part of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sports supporter in a throng; the supporter is a steel tower holding up cables.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall structure that holds up power lines.

clue.text: Company doing volte-face in lively dance number

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so those two letters swap round inside the dance word

parts.note: a cotillion is a lively dance of French origin

explanation.surface: A firm changes its mind halfway through a dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An octillion is a huge figure, a one followed by 27 zeros in the short scale.

clue.text: Rigorous person in market securing point

indicators.note: the word for market holds the point inside it

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork

explanation.surface: A strict figure at the market insists on making a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, named after a French drillmaster.

clue.text: Historic ship has the potential to succeed?

parts.note: to flower is to flourish, to succeed

explanation.surface: A question of whether a famous old vessel could thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower is the vessel that took English settlers to Plymouth, Massachusetts.

clue.text: Festering group in charge retaining power

indicators.note: the combined letters hold the power letter inside

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A corrupt ruling clique clings on to power.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic describes a wound infected and putrefying.

clue.text: City not entirely awash with money, receiving coin from oddball

indicators.note: the combined letters take the coin in between them

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for wealthy is dropped

explanation.surface: A not-quite-rich city takes in a coin from an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is a person of unconventional habits, a quirky sort.

clue.text: Beat to mash, mostly — satisfied?

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the word for mash

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether pounding food into mush is satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' reads like 'beat to a pulp' but is the past tense of the verb for a heart's rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulsated means throbbed rhythmically, as a heart beat.

clue.text: Showing regularity unknown at the beginning

explanation.surface: A habit that was mysterious from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly describes something recurring regularly, once every twelve months.

clue.text: Fruit and grain mostly in a container

indicators.note: the shortened grain goes inside the container
all but the last letter of the grain word

explanation.surface: A jar holding fruit and most of a cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is an orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Meeting Judge — purpose is to dismiss fine

indicators.note: the letter for fine is sent away from the purpose word

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: At a meeting, a judge intends to throw out a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction is a point where roads or lines meet.

clue.text: I competed to secure gold, displaying teeth?

indicators.note: the word for competed holds the gold inside

explanation.surface: A competitor goes for gold, grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivories is slang for teeth, so ivoried is a playful way of saying toothy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the stuff of tusks, and teeth are jokingly called ivories, so a toothy smile is ivoried.

clue.text: Monastery figure about to take up sinning?

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up turns the letters upward, backwards

explanation.surface: A monk on the verge of falling into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: A novice is a newcomer to a religious house, ironic as one about to sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationary member of a religious order living in a monastery.

clue.text: Clear criminal talent, working as a thief

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters of clear are twisted

parts.note: nous is common sense, practical talent

explanation.surface: A crook with an obvious flair for theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Larcenous means given to theft, larceny being the legal term for stealing.

clue.text: German city to wane in importance after dismissing leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the verb is removed

parts.note: to lessen is to decline or diminish

explanation.surface: A German city declines once its mayor is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, western Germany.

clue.text: Australian resort area: Australian willingly returning here

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: soon means willingly, as in I would as soon go

explanation.surface: An Australian is happy to go back to a favourite holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Noosa is a beach town on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, a popular Australian resort.

clue.text: Be ominous for Emperor (not half) and King

indicators.note: only the first half of the emperor's name is kept

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An omen concerning a half-dethroned emperor and a king.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to portend or foreshadow, as in augur ill.

clue.text: Illuminated points with expressions of approval (except the first)

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed

explanation.surface: Bright spots are marked with ticks, apart from the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicks are the burning tips of candles, points that are lit.

clue.text: Getting buried amongst Wagner's operas?

parts.note: the Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Someone is lost amid Wagner's lengthy operatic works.
explanation.definitionFit: Interring means burying a body in a grave.

clue.text: Followers regret holding on to European money

indicators.note: the regret word holds the other letters inside it

explanation.surface: Regret that one held on to euro cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the band of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Curtailed study applied to alcoholic drink, one's settled

definitions.note: noun phrase: something that settles a contest, with one's read as one is

indicators.note: cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: cider is alcoholic, made from apples

explanation.surface: A shortened study session with cider leaves one relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is the final game or point that settles the contest.
